summary: Steel lookout tower in Duplin County, NC, built by a CCC crew from Camp S-65 on March 10, 1937; no source read describes the site today.

facts.agency: North Carolina Division of Forest Resources

events.note: Constructed by a CCC crew from Camp S-65, dated March 10, 1937 in the Forest Lookouts entry.

evidence.supports: built March 1937 by a CCC crew from Camp S-65; 99-foot 9-inch steel tower
evidence.quote: March 10, 1937: A 99-foot 9-inch steel tower was constructed by a CCC.crew from Camp S-65.

notes_for_editor: The town named Pink Hill is in Lenoir County per Wikipedia, while the Forest Lookouts page and tnlandforms both list the tower in Duplin County; the story reports both and does not reconcile them. Two sources only (see above). No later history, staffing, fires or present-day condition was found. A listing on anyplaceamerica.com returned HTTP 403 and was not used. Not on FFLOS (its North Carolina register lists only Big Stamp and Frye Knob) or in the cached NHLR North Carolina list. The shared web-search budget for this run was exhausted before fate or present-day condition could be searched, and no other route was used. The record's agency field was null and is filled from the Forest Lookouts entry.
